record.paper_title: Supernomial Coefficients, Bailey's Lemma and Rogers-Ramanujan-Type Identities. A Survey of Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: For the A3 case, find a sufficiently simple closed expression for the more general summation sum_{L in Z_+^3} q^(L C L/2) S(L,k)/(q)_{M-L}, where M is an arbitrary element of Z_+^3, C is the A3 Cartan matrix, and S(L,k) is the normalized A3 supernomial. The expression should be simple enough, after any necessary extraction of common factors, to indicate how the A3 Bailey-type summation can be iterated beyond the isolated single-parameter A3 result sum_{L in Z_+^3} q^(L C L/2) S(L,k)/(q)_{M2-L2}.

evidence.quote: we have not found a sufficiently simple expression
to suggest how (after taking out possible factors) to iterate further

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $q$ be a formal variable and use the standard $q$-Pochhammer notation $(q)_n = \prod_{j=1}^n (1-q^j)$ for $n \in \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, with $(q)_n = 0$ for $n<0$ and the convention $1/(q)_{n}=0$ when $n<0$. For a vector $L=(L_1,L_2,L_3)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3$ and $M=(M_1,M_2,M_3)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3$, write $1/(q)_{M-L} = \prod_{i=1}^3 1/(q)_{M_i-L_i}$.

Let $C$ be the Cartan matrix of type $A_3$,
$$C=\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&0\\-1&2&-1\\0&-1&2\end{pmatrix},$$
and define the quadratic form $LCL/2 = \tfrac12\sum_{i,j}C_{ij}L_iL_j$.

For $L\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3$ and $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, let $S(L,k)$ denote the normalized $A_3$ supernomial coefficient: with $|L| = L_1+2L_2+3L_3$ assumed $\equiv 0\pmod{4}$ (otherwise $S(L,k)=0$), 
$$S(L,k) = \sum_{\substack{a,b,c,d\ge 0\\ a+b=L_1,\ c+d=L_2,\\ \text{(standard }A_3\text{ supernomial constraints)}}} \prod (\text{Gaussian }q\text{-binomials})$$
i.e. the $q$-supernomial associated with the symmetric power representation of weight $(k,k,k,\dots)$ for $\mathfrak{sl}_4$, normalized so that for the rank-one truncation it reduces to the Andrews--Bressoud $q$-supernomial.

Find a closed-form evaluation, simple enough that (after extracting common factors) it can be iterated as a Bailey-type recursion, of the multi-sum
$$F(M,k;q) \;=\; \sum_{L\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3} \frac{q^{LCL/2}\, S(L,k)}{(q)_{M_1-L_1}(q)_{M_2-L_2}(q)_{M_3-L_3}}, \qquad M=(M_1,M_2,M_3)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}^3.$$

The known case in which the denominator contains only the single factor $(q)_{M_2-L_2}$ (with no restriction on $L_1$ or $L_3$) admits a closed form; the problem is to obtain the analogous closed form for the full three-parameter sum above.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific A3 three-parameter Bailey-type summation involving the normalized A3 supernomial appears to be available; the question is posed as an open problem in the survey context, and a literature search did not turn up a subsequent paper providing the desired closed form.
